transcript: If you keep waking up between 3 and 4 am, your body may be warning you about something most people ignore. They blame it on needing to pee, but that is not always the real reason. Listen carefully. Many times, the problem is not your bladder, it is your nervous system. You go to sleep, but your body never truly feels safe. Your eyes are closed, but inside the mind is still running, thinking, planning, regretting, worrying about things you cannot control. And when the world becomes quiet, the thoughts you pushed away all day finally become loud. This is why you wake up at the same hour again and again. Not because the night is your enemy, but because your body is carrying too much into bed, too much stress, too much screen, too much unfinished emotion. And then people wake up, grab the phone, check the time, get angry and teach the body that 3 am is a time to panic. Do not do this. When you wake up, do not fight the night. Do not reach for the phone. Put one hand on your stomach and breathe slowly. Tell your body, I am safe. Nothing needs to be solved right now. Because sleep does not come to a body that feels chased. Sleep comes to a body that feels safe. If you want to calm your body and quiet your mind for the next 30 days, I put my 30-day healing journey in the link on my profile. Follow for more old monk healing lessons.
